clue.text: Dicky loved PE and what it enabled him to do

definitions.text: what it enabled him to do

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for shaky or unsound, so the words beside it are in poor order and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
physical education, taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy called Dicky enjoyed games lessons at school and they did him good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a boy's name but is the anagram signal. PE is physical education, the school sport lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Exercise lessons let a growing body build strength and grow, which is what the clue says they enabled.

clue.text: Hesitate to promote queer journalist

indicators.note: to promote is to raise, and in a down entry raising the letters means reading them from the bottom up

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Someone is reluctant to give an odd newspaper writer a promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection or show reluctance, a close synonym for holding back from acting.

clue.text: New arrival is "in vitro", perhaps

indicators.note: the small word is placed inside the Latin word that follows it
perhaps says the result is only one possible ordering, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newborn baby turns out to be a test-tube baby, conceived in vitro.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks invite you to read 'is in vitro' literally: the word is goes inside vitro, then the letters are rearranged into VISITOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor is someone who has just turned up at your door, a newcomer or new arrival.

clue.text: Sale item brings in nothing but money

indicators.note: to bring in is to take something inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a lot is an item put up at an auction sale
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: An auction piece earns nothing except cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Loot is informal slang for cash, as well as for stolen goods, so it can stand for money.

clue.text: Soldier on leave is no programmed item on Radio 3

parts.note: a private is the lowest rank of soldier

indicators.note: something programmed has been set up in a new order, so the two short words are rearranged

parts.note: a pass is a soldier's permit for leave
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier off duty hears that a planned item is not being broadcast on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Passions is a long-running BBC Radio 3 programme in which guests talk about the music they love. 'on' simply places one piece after another.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer names an actual BBC Radio 3 show, so it is literally a programme broadcast on that classical station.

clue.text: Disgusting bones scattered round the church

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the outside of the next piece
things scattered are thrown about in disorder, so the letters must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A grisly scene of human bones strewn around a churchyard.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene can mean offensive or repugnant, so it works as a synonym for revolting or disgusting.

clue.text: Theory of precision goes, if mutation occurs

indicators.note: a mutation is a change of form, so these letters change into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A scientist warns that exactness is lost when change creeps in.
explanation.walkthrough: Darwin's On the Origin of Species set out evolution by natural selection, in which mutation plays a part, so the anagram signal suits the subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Darwin's famous book sets out his evolutionary theory, so its short title stands for that theory.

clue.text: Favourite soft centre?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a darling or loved one
second meaning, split in two: the heart, or middle, of a sweet, which may be a soft centre

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer as SWEET HEART: the heart of a sweet, and soft centres are a classic kind of chocolate.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetheart is a beloved person, a favourite; and the core of a chocolate is literally the heart of a sweet.

clue.text: Antelope is no good out of the country

indicators.note: the animal's name lies outside the other piece, which sits within it

parts.note: the eland is a large African antelope
NG is the standard abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: An antelope is useless once removed from the open countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' reads as rural land, but it names a particular nation.
explanation.definitionFit: England is a nation within the United Kingdom, so it is a country.

clue.text: Way out, way out — one going out with a soldier

indicators.note: something going out leaves, so that letter departs from the word for an exit

parts.note: an exit is a way out
one is the Roman numeral I
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Someone escorts a soldier through the exit as they leave.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'way out' is used twice: first as slang for far-fetched, the definition, then literally as an exit.
explanation.definitionFit: Way out is slang for outlandish or far beyond the normal, which is what extreme means.

clue.text: Strength said to be found in one old dictator

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word for strength is used by its sound

parts.note: muscle is physical strength
taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A tyrant of the past is reputed to have been immensely powerful.
explanation.walkthrough: MUSCLE-IN-I spoken quickly sounds like Mussolini, the Fascist ruler of Italy from 1922 to 1943.
explanation.definitionFit: Benito Mussolini was Italy's Fascist leader before and during the Second World War, a historical tyrant.

clue.text: Reported serial attacker captured by the Queen

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
got means caught or captured

explanation.surface: A news story about a serial killer being arrested by the monarch herself.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like a serial killer, but 'serial' said aloud is cereal: ergot is a fungus attacking rye and other grain. 'by the Queen' puts her after the verb but her letters first.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergot is a fungal disease of rye and similar grain crops, so it literally attacks cereals.

clue.text: Routine is hard for a woman

parts.note: a rut is a dull, fixed routine
H is the pencil-lead abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A daily grind is tough on a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is a female given name, so it can stand for any woman in crossword convention.

clue.text: Beak spoils tart's image

indicators.note: to spoil something is to damage or disorder it, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A judge ruins a woman of doubtful reputation's public image.
explanation.walkthrough: Beak is British slang for a magistrate or judge, not a bird's bill.
explanation.definitionFit: In old British slang a beak is a magistrate, the lay judge sitting in a lower court.

clue.text: Shield able to provide little cover

indicators.note: the words are made to provide something new, that is reworked into a different arrangement

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A shield that offers hardly any protection.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is unusually weak: the words must be read as reworked to provide the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Deshabille is a state of being partly or scantily dressed, wearing very few clothes.

clue.text: Musical heard in the country

indicators.note: heard means listened to, so the show's title counts by its sound alone

parts.note: Grease is the 1970s stage and film musical

explanation.surface: A stage show is listened to out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Greece is a nation in south-east Europe, so it fits a country.

clue.text: Round the Cape and turn in late

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: the turn is put inside the name of the cape

parts.note: Cape Verde, the island nation off West Africa
a U-turn, so U for turn

explanation.surface: A ship rounds the headland and heads into port behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Cape' gives the second word of Cape Verde, the island group off West Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overdue has passed the time it was expected, so it is late.

clue.text: 14's money once grabbed by landlord — Rachman, for example

indicators.note: something grabbed is held inside, so the letters sit within the words that follow

parts.note: found across the end of the first word and most of the name

explanation.surface: A notorious slum landlord seizes a foreign tenant's old currency.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Rachman was a notoriously exploitative London slum landlord of the 1950s. 14 refers to the answer at 14-across, Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The drachma was the currency of Greece before the euro replaced it in 2002.

clue.text: One fed up with worker being bolshie

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
taken as written
the ant is the usual crossword worker

explanation.surface: Someone fed up with a colleague turns stroppy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed up' reads as one phrase meaning annoyed, but 'up' is the reversal signal. Bolshie is British slang for rebellious or uncooperative.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshie means stubbornly uncooperative and rebellious, which is close to openly resisting or defiant.

clue.text: Article dropped by runner in Georgia

definitions.note: a location phrase standing for a place in Georgia

indicators.note: the article is let fall by the mythical runner, so one of those letters goes

parts.note: Atalanta, the swift huntress of Greek myth who lost a race by stopping for golden apples
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece is discarded by an athlete somewhere in Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one A from the name of the fleet-footed Atalanta.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlanta is the capital city of the US state of Georgia, so it is a place there.

clue.text: Tories could be on the attack

indicators.note: could be suggests a possible alternative form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The Conservatives might go on the offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: Tories are members of the British Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A sortie is a sudden attack made by troops from a defended position.

clue.text: Creatures of trendy religious groups

parts.note: in means fashionable
sects are religious groups

explanation.surface: Followers of fashionable cults.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects are small six-legged animals, so they are living creatures.

clue.text: Horse-breaker, so to speak, delays proceedings

definitions.note: a verb phrase; the answer is the noun or the verb's base form

indicators.note: so to speak means when spoken, so the phrase counts by its sound

parts.note: a filly is a young mare and a buster is one who breaks in horses

explanation.surface: A bronco-buster holds up the business of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: A filibuster is a very long speech made to delay or block a vote in a legislature.
explanation.definitionFit: Filibustering is talking at length in a legislature to stall or obstruct business.

clue.text: Bones with great sex appeal

parts.note: OS is outsize, a clothing size for great
SA is the abbreviation for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A slim but very attractive figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Ossa is the Latin plural of os, bone, used in anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossa is the anatomical Latin plural for skeletal parts, so it means bones.

clue.text: Something deep Neddy's taken by

indicators.note: the animal has taken the little word in, so it sits inside

parts.note: Neddy is a pet name for a donkey
taken as written

explanation.surface: A donkey has been charmed by something profound.
explanation.walkthrough: Neddy is a British nickname for a donkey; read 'Neddy's' as Neddy has.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a bottomless chasm, a very deep hole or gulf.

clue.text: Creep on four legs

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to grovel or flatter servilely
second meaning: a young deer, a creature walking on all fours

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as crawling on hands and knees; the two senses are a verb for grovelling and a young deer.
explanation.definitionFit: To fawn is to grovel or toady; a fawn is also a young deer, which goes about on all fours.

clue.text: Write off article from periodical

indicators.note: the article is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: an annual is a yearly publication
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An editor cancels a piece from a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to cancel or declare void, as one might cancel a debt by writing it off.

clue.text: Cigar rolled in holy assembly of ruling clique

indicators.note: a rolled cigar has its leaf turned over and over, so these letters are mixed up
an assembly puts parts together in a new form, so the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone smokes a cigar in a church gathering of the powerful few.
explanation.definitionFit: An oligarchy is government by a small group, or that small ruling group itself.

clue.text: Playwright is very nearly cross

indicators.note: very nearly means not quite all of it, so the final letter of the word for crossing goes

parts.note: to traverse is to cross

explanation.surface: A dramatist is almost angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like angry, but is the verb to go across. Ben Travers wrote the Aldwych farces of the 1920s.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Travers was an English dramatist famous for his farces, so he is a playwright.

clue.text: Hollow cavities put to evil purposes

parts.note: sin is wickedness, evil
uses are purposes

explanation.surface: Empty spaces are being exploited for wicked ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinuses are the air-filled spaces in the skull bones behind the nose, so they are hollow cavities.
